items.prompt: Which letter is silent in the word lamb?

options.why: You can hear the l at the start of lamb.
You can hear the a sound in the middle of lamb.
You can hear the m sound at the end of lamb.

hints: Say lamb slowly and listen to each sound.
A silent letter is written but not heard.
Say the word and point to each letter as you hear its sound.
items.explanation: In lamb, the b is written but not heard. Other words with a silent b after m are thumb, climb and comb.

items.prompt: Which silent letter is missing? I gave the ___rong answer.
hints: The missing letter comes before r and makes no sound.
Think of other words that start with a silent letter before r, such as the joint between your hand and your arm.
Picture the word written down. What letter comes before the r?
items.explanation: Wrong starts with a silent w, like write, wrist and wrap.

items.prompt: Sort the words by their silent letter.
hints: Say each word aloud and listen for the letter you cannot hear.
Silent k and silent w often come at the start of a word. Silent b often comes after m.
Start with knee. Which letter is written but not heard?
items.explanation: Knee and knot have a silent k, wrist and wreck a silent w, thumb and climb a silent b, and honest and rhyme a silent h.

items.prompt: Choose the correct word. The children left ___ bags by the door.

options.why: There is about a place, as in over there.
They’re is short for they are.
Thier is a common misspelling. The e comes before the i.

hints: The missing word tells us who the bags belong to.
Try putting they are in the gap. If it does not make sense, it is not the short form.
Ask: whose bags? Then find the word that shows belonging.
items.explanation: Their shows that something belongs to them: their bags. There is a place, and they’re means they are.

items.prompt: Match each homophone to its meaning.
pairs: a calm time with no fighting
hints: Homophones sound the same but have different spellings and meanings.
Look for a smaller word or clue inside each spelling.
Start with piece. Think of a piece of pie: both words have pie in them.
items.explanation: A piece of pie is a part of it, and peace is calm. Weather is about the sky, whether means if, allowed means given permission and aloud means out loud.

items.prompt: Which word has a silent t?

options.why: You can hear the t sound in letter.
You can hear both t sounds in twist.
You can hear the first t. The second t is part of the shun sound.

hints: Say each word slowly.
A silent t is often found after s, as in castle.
Start with the first word. Do you hear every t in it? Then try the next word.
items.explanation: In listen, the t is not sounded. Castle, fasten and whistle also have a silent t after s.

items.prompt: Write the correct homophones. Please ___ a few minutes. The parcel’s ___ is four kilograms.
hints: The first gap is about time. The second gap is about how heavy something is.
One of the homophones is spelt like eight with a w at the front.
Start with the first gap: what do you do while time passes?
items.explanation: Wait means to stay until something happens. Weight is how heavy something is, spelt like eight with a w.

items.prompt: Which sentence uses the correct homophones?

options.text: The night rode through the knight to reach the castle.
options.why: A knight is a soldier on horseback, and night is the time when it is dark.

options.text: The knight road through the night to reach the castle.
options.why: Road is a street. The past tense of ride is rode.

options.text: The knight rode through the night to reach the castle.
The knight rode threw the night to reach the castle.
options.why: Threw is the past tense of throw. Through means from one side to the other.

hints: Each sentence has the same words except for some homophones.
Check each homophone one at a time against its meaning.
Start with the person on the horse. Which spelling means a soldier on horseback?
items.explanation: A knight is a soldier on horseback, rode is the past tense of ride, through means from one side to the other and night is when it is dark.

items.prompt: Choose all the words that have a silent letter.

options.why: Every letter in plant is sounded.
Every letter in brush is sounded. Sh makes one sound.
Every letter in lemon is sounded.

hints: Say each word slowly and listen for letters you cannot hear.
Silent letters can hide in the middle of words too, for example after s or g.
Start with the first word. Say it slowly and point to each letter as you hear it.
items.explanation: Doubt has a silent b, guess has a silent u after g, and scissors has a silent c after the first s.

items.prompt: Which word has no silent letter?

options.why: The k at the start of knowledge is silent.
The l in salmon is silent. Say it: sam-un.
The c and h in yacht are silent. Say it: yot.

hints: Three of the words hide a silent letter somewhere.
Say each word slowly and match each letter to a sound.
Start with yacht. How many letters can you actually hear?
items.explanation: Every letter in basket is sounded. Knowledge has a silent k, salmon has a silent l and yacht has a silent c and h.

items.prompt: Which word sounds the same as sun, but means a boy child?

options.why: Sum is an answer to an addition. It sounds different.
Soon means in a short time and has a longer sound.
Sung is the past of sing. It ends with ng.

hints: Homophones sound the same but are spelled differently.
Say sun aloud and listen to each word.
The word is a family word.
items.explanation: Son and sun are homophones. A son is a boy child.

items.prompt: ___ going to the beach on Saturday.
hints: Try saying the sentence with they are.
They’re is short for they are.
Their shows belonging and there shows a place.
items.explanation: They’re means they are. Their shows ownership and there shows a place.

items.prompt: Write the silent letter that starts the word. A ___nome lives in the garden.
hints: Gnomes are tiny garden figures.
The first letter is not said.
Say the word. You hear nome, so a letter is hidden before the n.
items.explanation: Gnome is said nome. The g is silent.

items.prompt: Sort the words by their silent letter.
hints: Say each word slowly and notice the letter you cannot hear.
Three letters are hiding: b, k and w.
Climb and thumb end with the same silent letter.
items.explanation: The b is silent in climb and thumb, the k in knock and knight, and the w in wrap and wrist.

items.prompt: Match each homophone to its meaning.
hints: Homophones sound the same, so use the meaning.
Here and there are both places.
Hear has the word ear inside it.
items.explanation: Hear has ear in it. Here is a place. Sea is water, and see is what eyes do.

items.prompt: Build the sentence.
items.answer: There are two books on their desk.
hints: The sentence starts with a word that tells a place.
The word for belonging comes before desk.
Put the number word after are.
items.explanation: There starts the sentence, two is the number, and their shows the desk belongs to them.

items.prompt: The twins left ___ lunch boxes at home, so ___ hungry. They hope ___ is a shop nearby.
hints: Check each gap by trying they are in it.
Their shows belonging to people.
There can show a place or be used with is and are.
items.explanation: The first gap shows belonging (their). The second means they are (they’re). The third is a place (there).

items.prompt: Spell the word for pens, paper and envelopes.
items.sentence: Citra bought stationery for the new school year.
hints: This word is a noun for writing things.
It ends with ery, like the e in envelope.
The other word, with ary, means not moving.
items.explanation: Stationery with an e means paper and pens. Stationary with an a means not moving.

items.prompt: Which word has a silent letter that is NOT at the start?

options.why: The g at the start is silent.
The w at the start is silent.
The k at the start is silent.

hints: Check where the silent letter sits in each word.
Three of the words have a silent letter first.
Say island: eye-land. Which letter in the middle is missing in the sound?
items.explanation: In island the s is silent, in the middle of the word.

items.prompt: Which sentence uses stationary correctly?

options.text: Putri bought new stationary for school.
options.why: Stationary means not moving. Pens and paper are stationery.

options.text: Hadi packed his stationary into a case.
options.why: Stationary means not moving. Pens and paper are stationery.

options.text: The bus was stationary at the red light.
She sells stationary in her shop.
options.why: Stationary means not moving. Pens and paper are stationery.

hints: Stationary with an a means not moving.
Think: Does the sentence talk about something not moving?
Look for the sentence about a vehicle waiting.
items.explanation: Stationary means still. Stationery with an e means writing materials.

items.prompt: Choose all the sentences that use the correct homophone.

options.why: Herd is a group of animals. You hear with your ears, so use heard.

options.text: Leo ate a piece of cake.

options.why: No is the opposite of yes. Use know for knowing something.

options.text: She threw the ball over the fence.

options.why: Road is a path. The past of ride is rode.

hints: Check each sentence for a word that sounds right but means something else.
Three sentences are correct.
Say what each tricky word should mean, then match it to its spelling.
items.explanation: Piece of cake, weather, and threw the ball are all correct. The other sentences use the wrong homophone.

items.prompt: Write the right homophone of rain for each gap. The old king’s ___ lasted forty years. The rider held the ___ tightly.
hints: Both words sound like rain.
The first word is about being a ruler.
The second word is a strap on a horse.
items.explanation: Reign means the time a king rules. A rein is a strap used to steer a horse.

items.prompt: Which sentence uses every homophone correctly?

options.text: Ines past the shop on her way hear.
options.why: Past should be passed here, and hear should be here.

options.text: The sail on the boat was to big for the wind.
options.why: To should be too.

options.text: Citra lent her pencil to a pupil who’s pencil broke.
options.why: Who’s means who is. Use whose to show belonging.

options.text: Tom threw the whole cake in the bin because it was stale.

hints: Check every tricky word in each sentence.
Look for past/passed, hear/here, to/too and who’s/whose.
Only one sentence has no mistakes at all.
items.explanation: Threw, whole and stale are all correct in the right sentence. The others have wrong homophones.

items.prompt: Which pair of words are NOT homophones?

options.why: They sound the same.
They sound the same.
They sound the same.

hints: Homophones sound exactly the same.
Say each pair aloud.
Listen for the last sound of each word.
items.explanation: Lose ends with a z sound and loose ends with an s sound, so they sound different.
